text: How empty the city, once teeming with people. A widow, this city, once in the front rank of nations, once queen of the ball, she's now a drudge in the kitchen.
No one's left among her lovers to sit and hold her hand. Her friends have all dumped her.
She camps out among the nations, never feels at home. Hunted by all, she's stuck between a rock and a hard place.
All her city gates are deserted, her priests in despair. Her virgins are sad. How bitter her fate.
because God laid her low, punishing her repeated rebellions. Her children, prisoners of the enemy, trudge into exile.
Her princes are like deer famished for food, chased to exhaustion by hunters.
when her people fell into enemy hands, and not a soul there to help. Enemies looked on and laughed, laughed at her helpless silence.
All who admired her despise her now that they see beneath the surface. Miserable, she groans and turns away in shame.
and now she's crashed royally, with no one to hold her hand: "Look at my pain, O God! And how the enemy cruelly struts."
as pagans barged into her Sanctuary, those very people for whom you posted orders: keep out: this assembly off-limits.
that they bartered their favorite things for a bit of breakfast: "O God, look at me! Worthless, cheap, abject!
Ever seen pain like my pain, seen what he did to me, what God did to me in his rage?
then he set traps all around so I could hardly move. He left me with nothing—left me sick, and sick of living.
and harnessed me to captivity's yoke. I'm goaded by cruel taskmasters.
then called in thugs to break their fine young necks. The Master crushed the life out of fair virgin Judah.
and not a soul within miles around cares for my soul. My children are wasted, my enemy got his way."
God ordered Jacob's enemies to surround him, and now no one wants anything to do with Jerusalem.
Listen everybody! Look at what I'm going through! My fair young women, my fine young men, all herded into exile!
My priests and my leaders only looked after themselves, trying but failing to save their own skins.
my heart wrecked by a life of rebellion. Massacres in the streets, starvation in the houses.
When my enemies heard of the trouble you gave me, they cheered. Bring on Judgment Day! Let them get what I got!
Give them what you gave me for my sins. Groaning in pain, body and soul, I've had all I can take."
